questions.question: A bag contains 4 red, 3 blue, and 5 green balls. What is the probability of drawing a blue ball?
Two dice are rolled. What is the probability of getting a sum of 7?
What is the probability of drawing an ace from a standard deck of 52 cards?
questions.tutor: There are 4 aces in a 52-card deck. P = 4/52 = 1/13.

questions.question: If P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.3 and A and B are mutually exclusive, what is P(A∪B)?
questions.tutor: For mutually exclusive events: P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7.

questions.question: A coin is tossed 3 times. What is the probability of getting exactly 2 heads?
If P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, and P(A∩B) = 0.2, what is P(A∪B)?
A box has 6 defective and 14 good items. What is the probability of picking 2 good items without replacement?
What is the probability of getting at least one head when tossing a coin twice?
questions.tutor: P(at least one head) = 1 - P(no heads) = 1 - (1/2)² = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4.

questions.question: In a class of 30 students, 18 like Math and 15 like Science, 10 like both. How many like neither?
If events A and B are independent with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.5, what is P(A∩B)?
questions.tutor: For independent events: P(A∩B) = P(A) × P(B) = 0.3 × 0.5 = 0.15.
